gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-glago: Capture It towers over the line with a tall, urban stance. Noto Sans Glagolitic is a plain sans with round, open letters that stay clear at small sizes, so the heading's nearly sealed shapes get a relaxed partner underneath.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-gothi: Capture It stands tall and commanding, its letters nearly sealed shut. Noto Sans Gothic loosens everything beside it, with big glassy counters and rounded forms like open parentheses, which makes the two feel like a shout and a breath.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-grant: Noto Sans Grantha runs tall and small-bowled, never snagging on a closed-up shape. Capture It, though, is the tight one, its towering display letters almost sealed, so the sans body reads as the easy exhale after them.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-gujar: Noto Sans Gujarati reads as a plain sans, its curved strokes stopping short of turning inward and leaving big open counters. Capture It is built to command with stress-free curves; the body is built to be read.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-gunja: Towering lowercase with nearly sealed shapes gives Capture It its urban bite. Against it, Noto Sans Gunjala Gondi is a plain sans with cut-back terminals and wide gaps, and that open-versus-closed tension is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-gurmu: Commanding and urban, Capture It sits tall with its letters nearly shut. Noto Sans Gurmukhi is a sans with outward-pointing terminals and low ascenders, and it gives that tightness somewhere open to land on the page.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-hanun: Capture It brings a towering x-height and barely any opening in its letters. And Noto Sans Hanunoo, a sans-serif with lowercase filling most of the height and open terminals, makes that closed-versus-open contrast the pair's strongest quality.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-hebre: Noto Sans Hebrew reads with a dominant midsection and wide gaps between curve ends and stems. And Capture It, closed up and uniform in stroke, even down to the tail of its y, gives that openness a sharp, urban counterpart.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-hk: Big, blunt, nearly sealed shut. Noto Sans HK, a sans-serif with large lowercase and brush ends lifted before each curve closes, lets Capture It's urban weight sit above it without crowding the page.
gen-dafont-capture-it-gf-noto-sans-imper: Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic reads as a sans with c ends pointing apart like pincers and capitals barely taller than lowercase. But Capture It is the closed-up one, with no thick-thin variation, so the two sit together as tight and open.
